title: King Parakramabahu I
biography: Parakramabahu I (1153–1186), known as 'Parakramabahu the Great,' is Polonnaruwa's most celebrated monarch. His 33-year reign transformed the capital into a hydraulic and architectural marvel: constructing the massive Parakrama Samudra reservoir, magnificent palace complexes, and ornate Buddhist temples (Vatadage, Lankathilaka). He unified fractious regional kingdoms, conducted military campaigns into South India and Burma, and patronized literature and the arts. His famous maxim—'Not a drop of water should reach the sea without serving man'—epitomizes his hydraulic vision. His reign represents Polonnaruwa's zenith: political unity, economic prosperity, and cultural brilliance.

title: King Siva II
biography: Siva II ruled Anuradhapura for nine years during a period of complex dynastic politics. He maintained Buddhist patronage and irrigation, navigating factional disputes among rival claimants. His reign exemplifies the challenges of sustaining kingship amid frequent succession struggles.

title: Pharaoh Djoser (Netjerikhet)
kingdom: Old Kingdom of Egypt (Age of the Pyramids)
biography: Second pharaoh of the Third Dynasty who commissioned royal architect Imhotep to construct the world's first colossal stone building: the Step Pyramid of Saqqara.
internationalConnections: Organized major mining expeditions to the Sinai peninsula for turquoise and copper.

title: King Kanakasuriya Cinkaiariyan
biography: Kanakasuriya Cinkaiariyan ruled Jaffna for 17 years under Kotte's overlordship until Parakramabahu VI's death. He reasserted autonomy after 1467, revitalizing Hindu institutions and trade. His reign marks Jaffna's recovery of independence in the kingdom's twilight.

title: Yongle Emperor (Zhu Di)
biography: Visionary Ming emperor who moved the capital to Beijing, constructed the Forbidden City, rebuilt the Grand Canal, compiled the Yongle Encyclopedia, and sponsored Admiral Zheng He's seven epic maritime treasure voyages.
internationalConnections: Zheng He's treasure fleet established diplomatic ties with Sri Lanka (Kotte), India (Calicut), Hormuz, and East Africa (Malindi).

title: King Karaliyadde Bandara
biography: Karaliyadde Bandara's 29-year reign witnessed increasing Portuguese pressure on Kandy and the rise of Sitawaka. He preserved the Tooth Relic and Buddhist traditions amid regional warfare. Factional intrigue ended his reign, though the kingdom's independence survived.
